cards.t: The main query cannot retrieve data from a subquery
cards.tz: 主查询不能取用子查询的字段
cards.en:
Intuition: a subquery is like asking a friend a yes/no or a list question. You get the answer, not their notebook. Fields inside the subquery are invisible to the main query.

✗ SELECT NAME, h.NAME FROM BREED WHERE ID IN (SELECT BID FROM CAT, HOTEL h WHERE …) → error: h does not exist outside the brackets.

  • A subquery only supplies values for filtering (or one calculated value).
  • If the output needs fields from several tables, join them in the main query.
  • The other direction is allowed: a correlated subquery can use the outer query's fields.

Exam wording: The main query cannot retrieve data from the subquery; tables must be joined in the main query if their fields are to be displayed.
cards.zh:
直觉：子查询像问朋友一个问题，你只拿到答案，看不到他的笔记。子查询里的字段对主查询是看不见的。

✗ 在主查询 SELECT h.NAME → 出错，h 只存在于括号内。

  • 子查询只为过滤提供值（或一个计算值）。
  • 要显示多个表的字段，要在主查询连接。
  • 反方向可以：相关子查询可以用外层字段。

要背：The main query cannot retrieve data from the subquery; tables must be joined in the main query if their fields are to be displayed.

ex.q: Show each cat's name with its hotel's name.
ex.a:
1. Both names must be displayed → both tables in the main query.
  2. SELECT c.NAME, h.NAME AS HNAME FROM CAT c JOIN HOTEL h ON c.HID = h.ID.
  3. 7 cats (Bean has no hotel and is dropped).
ex.az:
1. 两个名字都要显示 → 主查询连接。
  2. JOIN HOTEL。
  3. 7 只猫。

ex.q: Can a subquery be used in the SELECT list?
ex.a:
1. Yes, if it returns one value (scalar subquery).
  2. e.g. SELECT NAME, (SELECT AVG(WEIGHT) FROM CAT) AS AVGW FROM CAT.
  3. It still cannot expose its inner table to the main query.
ex.az:
1. 可以，只要返回一个值。
  2. 例子见左边。
  3. 仍不能让主查询用它内部的表。

ex.q: A student writes SELECT NAME, HNAME FROM CAT WHERE HID IN (SELECT ID AS HNAME FROM HOTEL). Why does it fail?
ex.a:
1. HNAME is an alias inside the subquery only.
  2. The main query (CAT) has no field HNAME → error.
  3. Join CAT and HOTEL instead.
ex.az:
1. HNAME 只在子查询内。
  2. 主查询找不到 → 出错。
  3. 改用连接。

demo.query:
SELECT c.NAME, h.NAME AS HNAME
FROM CAT c JOIN HOTEL h ON c.HID = h.ID;
demo.note: To display fields of two tables, join them in the main query.

cards.t: Correlated subqueries: comparing with the outer row
cards.tz: 相关子查询：与外层的行比较
cards.en:
Intuition: "Is this cat heavier than the average of its own breed?" The average changes for each cat, so the subquery must be run for each cat.

SELECT NAME FROM CAT c
WHERE WEIGHT > (SELECT AVG(WEIGHT) FROM CAT c2
                WHERE c2.BID = c.BID)
  • Use a second alias (c2) for the same table inside the subquery.
  • c2.BID = c.BID links "the group" to "the current row".
  • Count without GROUP BY: WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM CAT WHERE HID = h.ID) > CAPACITY.
  • Sometimes a simple join is easier, e.g. compare c.WEIGHT with BREED's stored average b.WEIGHT.

Exam wording: A correlated subquery uses a field of the main query, so it is evaluated for each record of the main query.
cards.zh:
直觉：“这只猫比它自己品种的平均体重重吗？”每只猫的平均值不同，所以子查询要每只猫执行一次。

  • 同一表在子查询里用第二个别名（c2）。
  • c2.BID = c.BID 把“组”连到“当前行”。
  • 不用 GROUP BY 也能计数：子查询 COUNT 后与 CAPACITY 比较。
  • 有时连接更简单。

要背：A correlated subquery uses a field of the main query, so it is evaluated for each record of the main query.

ex.q: Which cats are heavier than their own breed's average? Trace Ragdolls.
ex.a:
1. Ragdolls: Mochi 7.0, Luna 5.8, Nala 6.0 → average 6.27.
  2. Mochi 7.0 > 6.27 ✓; Luna ✗; Nala ✗.
  3. Do the same for each breed (see demo).
ex.az:
1. Ragdoll 平均 6.27。
  2. 只有 Mochi 超过。
  3. 其他品种同理。

ex.q: Hotels with more cats than capacity, without GROUP BY.
ex.a:
1. For each hotel h, count cats: (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM CAT WHERE HID = h.ID).
  2. Alpha 4 > 3 ✓; Beta 2 > 2 ✗; Gamma 1 > 4 ✗.
  3. Result: Alpha.
ex.az:
1. 每间酒店数猫。
  2. Alpha 4 > 3。
  3. 结果：Alpha。

ex.q: A student writes the subquery without c2: (SELECT AVG(WEIGHT) FROM CAT WHERE BID = BID). Result?
ex.a:
1. BID = BID compares the inner row with itself → always TRUE.
  2. The subquery gives the average of all cats, not the breed.
  3. Use a second alias and c2.BID = c.BID.
ex.az:
1. BID = BID 永远成立。
  2. 得到的是全部猫的平均。
  3. 要用 c2.BID = c.BID。

demo.note: For each cat, the subquery averages only cats of the same breed.

code.src:
SELECT NAME FROM HOTEL h
WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM CAT
       WHERE HID = h.ID)
      > CAPACITY;

notes.t: Show hotel names (outer alias h).
notes.tz: 显示酒店名，外层别名 h。

notes.t: For this hotel, count the cats …
… whose HID is this hotel's ID (correlated).
Keep the hotel if the count is over capacity.

code.out:
NAME
-----
Alpha

cards.t: 'Does not have': use NOT IN, not <>
cards.en:
Intuition: "hotels with no Ragdoll". If you join and say breed <> Ragdoll, you only drop the Ragdoll rows. Alpha still has a Persian row, so Alpha sneaks in.

  • ✗ … WHERE b.NAME <> 'Ragdoll' → hotels with at least one non-Ragdoll cat.
  • ✓ WHERE ID NOT IN (SELECT HID FROM CAT c, BREED b WHERE c.BID = b.ID AND b.NAME = 'Ragdoll')
  • First find who has it, then take everyone else.

Exam wording: To find records that do not have a value, use NOT IN / NOT EXISTS with a subquery that finds the records that have it.
cards.zh:
直觉：“没有 Ragdoll 的酒店”。连接后写 <> 'Ragdoll' 只去掉 Ragdoll 那几行，Alpha 仍有 Persian 行，所以 Alpha 混进来了。

  • ✗ <> → 至少有一只非 Ragdoll 的酒店。
  • ✓ 先找出有 Ragdoll 的酒店，再用 NOT IN。

要背：To find records that do not have a value, use NOT IN / NOT EXISTS with a subquery that finds the records that have it.

ex.q: Hotels without Ragdolls (data in demo).
ex.a:
1. Hotels with Ragdolls: Mochi, Nala → Alpha; Luna → Beta.
  2. NOT IN (1, 2).
  3. Result: Gamma.
ex.az:
1. 有 Ragdoll：Alpha、Beta。
  2. NOT IN。
  3. Gamma。

ex.q: Students who are not in Science Club.
ex.a:
1. Who is in Science Club: SID IN SC with CID 4.
  2. STUDENT WHERE SID NOT IN (that list).
  3. Ada, Finn, Ben. (Clem is excluded even though she is also in Chess.)
ex.az:
1. 先找 Science Club 成员。
  2. NOT IN。
  3. Ada、Finn、Ben。

ex.q: A student writes SELECT DISTINCT s.NAME FROM STUDENT s, SC WHERE s.SID = SC.SID AND CID <> 4. Why is Clem wrongly listed?
ex.a:
1. Clem has rows with CID 1, 2 and 4.
  2. Rows 1 and 2 pass CID <> 4, so Clem appears.
  3. Use NOT IN with a subquery. (Ben is also wrongly missing, since he has no SC row.)
ex.az:
1. Clem 有 CID 1、2 的行。
  2. 这些行通过条件。
  3. 要用 NOT IN；Ben 也被漏掉。

demo.note: First find hotels that HAVE a Ragdoll, then take the others.

cards.en:
Intuition: a hotel with 3 Persians has only 1 breed of Persian. DISTINCT counts each different value once.

SELECT h.NAME, COUNT(DISTINCT c.BID)
FROM HOTEL h LEFT JOIN CAT c ON h.ID = c.HID
GROUP BY h.ID
  • LEFT JOIN with HOTEL on the left → every hotel listed.
  • DISTINCT c.BID → each breed counted once per hotel.
  • Empty hotel: BID is NULL, COUNT ignores NULL → 0.

Exam wording: COUNT(DISTINCT field) counts the number of different non-NULL values; the statement counts the number of different cat breeds within each hotel.
cards.zh:
直觉：有 3 只 Persian 的酒店，Persian 这个品种只算 1 个。DISTINCT 让相同值只数一次。

  • HOTEL 在左 LEFT JOIN → 每间酒店都列出。
  • DISTINCT c.BID → 每种品种算一次。
  • 空酒店 BID 为 NULL → 0。

要背：COUNT(DISTINCT field) counts the number of different non-NULL values; the statement counts the number of different cat breeds within each hotel.

ex.q: Count breeds per hotel (data in demo).
ex.a:
1. Alpha BIDs: 1, 2, 3, 1 → 3 different.
  2. Beta: 1, 2 → 2. Gamma: 2 → 1.
  3. Add an empty hotel and it shows 0.
ex.az:
1. Alpha 3 种。
  2. Beta 2，Gamma 1。
  3. 空酒店 0。

ex.q: Number of different clubs joined by students of each class.
ex.a:
1. STUDENT s LEFT JOIN SC ON s.SID = SC.SID.
  2. GROUP BY CLASS; COUNT(DISTINCT CID).
  3. 3A: Ada(2), Ben(none) → 1; 3B: Clem(1,2,4), Eva(4), Finn(1) → 3; 3C: 4 → 1.
ex.az:
1. 连接后按班分组。
  2. COUNT(DISTINCT CID)。
  3. 3A 1、3B 3、3C 1。

ex.q: A student uses COUNT(c.BID) without DISTINCT. What does Alpha show?
ex.a:
1. COUNT counts every non-NULL BID: 1, 2, 3, 1 → 4.
  2. That is the number of cats, not breeds.
  3. Add DISTINCT → 3.
ex.az:
1. 数了 4 个 BID。
  2. 那是猫的数目。
  3. 加 DISTINCT → 3。

demo.note: Compare: BREEDS counts different breeds, CATS counts cats. Delta is empty → 0.

cards.t: Join vs subquery: rewriting between them
cards.tz: 连接 vs 子查询：互相改写
cards.en:
Intuition: many questions can be solved either way. Pick the one that is clearer.

NeedBetter
Display fields from 2+ tablesJoin
Compare with an aggregate (above average, the max)Subquery
"does not have …"NOT IN / NOT EXISTS
Avoid duplicates from one-to-many rowsSubquery (or DISTINCT)

Rewrite pattern: WHERE x IN (SELECT y FROM T WHERE cond) ≈ JOIN T ON x = y WHERE cond + DISTINCT.

Exam wording: A join is needed when fields from more than one table are displayed; a subquery is suitable when the condition depends on the result of another query.
cards.zh:
直觉：很多题两种方法都可以，选清楚的一种。

需要较好
显示多个表的字段连接
与聚合值比较子查询
“没有……”NOT IN / NOT EXISTS
避免一对多造成重复子查询（或 DISTINCT）

改写模式：IN 子查询 ≈ JOIN + DISTINCT。

要背：A join is needed when fields from more than one table are displayed; a subquery is suitable when the condition depends on the result of another query.

ex.q: Rewrite with a join: SELECT NAME FROM STUDENT WHERE SID IN (SELECT SID FROM SC WHERE CID IN (1, 4))
ex.a:
1. JOIN SC ON STUDENT.SID = SC.SID WHERE CID IN (1, 4).
  2. Clem is in both clubs → appears twice.
  3. Add DISTINCT: SELECT DISTINCT NAME … → Clem, Eva, Gabe, Finn, Dio.
ex.az:
1. JOIN SC。
  2. Clem 出现两次。
  3. 加 DISTINCT。

ex.q: Show names of Chess Club members and the club's room. Join or subquery?
ex.a:
1. Room is in CLUB, name in STUDENT → both displayed.
  2. Must join (three tables).
  3. Subquery alone cannot show ROOM.
ex.az:
1. 两表字段都要显示。
  2. 要连接。
  3. 子查询做不到。

ex.q: A student rewrites the IN query as a join but forgets DISTINCT and says the counts match. Do they?
ex.a:
1. The IN version returns 5 names.
  2. The join version returns 6 rows (Clem twice).
  3. Different! Add DISTINCT (or keep IN).
ex.az:
1. IN 版本 5 个。
  2. 连接版本 6 行。
  3. 不同，要 DISTINCT。

demo.note: Remove DISTINCT to see Clem twice.

cards.en:
Intuition: joins glue tables side by side (more columns). Set operators stack results on top of each other (more rows), like merging two name lists.

SELECT SID, NAME FROM STUDENT
UNION
SELECT SID, NAME FROM STUDENT2
  • The SELECTs must have the same number of columns with compatible data types, in the same order.
  • Column names in the result come from the first SELECT.
  • UNION returns all rows of both results and removes duplicated rows.
  • Only rows that are completely identical (every selected column the same) count as duplicates.

Exam wording: UNION combines the results of two queries and removes duplicated records; the queries must have the same number of fields with compatible data types.
cards.zh:
直觉：JOIN 把表左右拼（多了字段）；集合运算把结果上下叠（多了行），像合并两张名单。

  • 各个 SELECT 要有相同数目的字段、兼容的数据类型、相同次序。
  • 结果的字段名来自第一个 SELECT。
  • UNION 合并并去除重复行。
  • 只有完全相同的行才算重复。

要背：UNION combines the results of two queries and removes duplicated records; the queries must have the same number of fields with compatible data types.

ex.q: STUDENT has 7 rows, STUDENT2 has 4 (Eva is in both, same SID and NAME). How many rows from the UNION of SID, NAME?
ex.a:
1. 7 + 4 = 11 rows before removing duplicates.
  2. Eva ('03505','Eva') appears twice → keep one.
  3. 10 rows.
ex.az:
1. 先 11 行。
  2. Eva 重复。
  3. 10 行。

ex.q: UNION of SELECT NAME, SCORE from both tables. Eva has 83 in both; Xing also has 83. How many 83s remain?
ex.a:
1. Eva–83 and Eva–83: identical → one kept.
  2. Xing–83 differs in NAME → kept.
  3. Two rows with 83.
ex.az:
1. Eva 两行相同 → 留一行。
  2. Xing 名字不同 → 保留。
  3. 两行 83。

ex.q: A student writes SELECT SID, NAME FROM STUDENT UNION SELECT SID FROM STUDENT2. Problem?
ex.a:
1. The first SELECT has 2 columns, the second has 1.
  2. Set operators need the same number of columns → error.
  3. Select the same fields in both.
ex.az:
1. 字段数目不同。
  2. → 出错。
  3. 两边选相同字段。

demo.note: 11 rows stacked; Eva's duplicate row removed → 10.

code.src:
SELECT NAME, SCORE FROM STUDENT
UNION
SELECT NAME, SCORE FROM STUDENT2
ORDER BY SCORE DESC;

notes.t: First result: names and scores of STUDENT.
Stack the results and remove identical rows.
Second result: same two columns from STUDENT2.
notes.tz: 第二个结果，同样两个字段。

notes.t: Sort the combined result (ORDER BY goes at the very end).
notes.tz: 对整个结果排序（放最后）。

code.out:
NAME  SCORE
----  -----
Clem  89
Ben   86
Eva   83
Xing  83
Dio   67
Zack  60
Gabe  47
Yen   47
Finn  35
Ada   0

cards.t: WHERE and ORDER BY in combined results
cards.tz: 合并结果中的 WHERE 和 ORDER BY
cards.en:
Intuition: each SELECT is its own little query with its own filter. The final sort applies to the whole stack, so it is written once, at the end.

  • WHERE belongs to each SELECT. To filter both parts, write WHERE in both.
  • ORDER BY can appear only once, after the last SELECT, and sorts the whole combined result.
  • Sort by a column name from the first SELECT (or its alias).
SELECT NAME FROM STUDENT WHERE SEX = 'F'
UNION
SELECT NAME FROM STUDENT2 WHERE SEX = 'F'
ORDER BY NAME

Exam wording: A WHERE clause only applies to its own SELECT statement; ORDER BY is placed at the end and sorts the combined result.
cards.zh:
直觉：每个 SELECT 有自己的过滤条件；最后的排序作用于整个结果，所以只写一次，放在最后。

  • WHERE 只属于它自己的 SELECT，两边都要过滤就两边都写。
  • ORDER BY 只能出现一次，放最后。
  • 用第一个 SELECT 的字段名（或别名）排序。

要背：A WHERE clause only applies to its own SELECT statement; ORDER BY is placed at the end and sorts the combined result.

ex.q: List girls from both tables, sorted by name.
ex.a:
1. WHERE SEX = 'F' in both SELECTs.
  2. UNION.
  3. ORDER BY NAME at the end → Ada, Clem, Eva, Yen.
ex.az:
1. 两边都写 WHERE。
  2. UNION。
  3. 最后排序。

ex.q: Only the second SELECT has WHERE SEX = 'F'. Who appears?
ex.a:
1. First part: all 7 STUDENT rows (boys too).
  2. Second part: Eva, Yen.
  3. So boys of STUDENT are included — probably not intended.
ex.az:
1. 第一部分 7 人全部。
  2. 第二部分只有女生。
  3. 男生也混进来。

ex.q: A student writes ORDER BY after the first SELECT and before UNION. Result?
ex.a:
1. ORDER BY is only allowed at the end of the whole statement.
  2. → syntax error.
  3. Move it to the end.
ex.az:
1. ORDER BY 只能放最后。
  2. 语法错误。
  3. 移到最后。

demo.query:
SELECT NAME FROM STUDENT WHERE SEX = 'F'
UNION
SELECT NAME FROM STUDENT2 WHERE SEX = 'F'
ORDER BY NAME;
demo.note: Each part has its own WHERE; one ORDER BY sorts the whole stack.

cards.tz: 连接表 vs 合并结果
cards.en:
Intuition: JOIN = wider (adds columns from another table, matched by a key). Set operator = longer (adds rows from another query with the same columns).

JOINUNION / INTERSECT / EXCEPT
Result growssideways (columns)downwards (rows)
Needsa join condition (related fields)same number of columns, compatible types
Typical usestudent + club detailsstudents from two schools in one list

Exam wording: Joining tables combines fields of related records; set operators combine the records of query results with the same structure.
cards.zh:
直觉：JOIN = 变宽（按 key 加入另一表的字段）；集合运算 = 变长（加入另一查询的行，字段相同）。

JOIN集合运算
结果横向加字段纵向加行
需要连接条件相同字段数、兼容类型

要背：Joining tables combines fields of related records; set operators combine the records of query results with the same structure.

ex.q: Show every student's name and their club's room. JOIN or UNION?
ex.a:
1. Name and room are different fields of related tables.
  2. → JOIN (wider).
ex.az:
1. 不同表的相关字段。
  2. → JOIN。

ex.q: One list of names of students in STUDENT and STUDENT2. JOIN or UNION?
ex.a:
1. Same structure, more rows.
  2. → UNION (longer).
ex.az:
1. 结构相同，多了行。
  2. → UNION。

ex.q: A student tries STUDENT JOIN STUDENT2 ON STUDENT.SID = STUDENT2.SID to get all students from both tables. Result?
ex.a:
1. The join keeps only SIDs in both tables → just Eva.
  2. And it puts the fields side by side.
  3. Use UNION to stack the lists.
ex.az:
1. 只保留两表都有的 SID → Eva。
  2. 还是横向排列。
  3. 应用 UNION。

frames.en: STUDENT + CLUB side by side: each row gets more columns (NAME … ROOM).
STUDENT rows on top of STUDENT2 rows: more rows, same columns.
frames.zh: 上下叠：行变多，字段相同。

cards.en:
Intuition: UNION is a careful clerk who removes duplicates. UNION ALL just staples the lists together; faster, keeps everything.

  • UNION ALL keeps duplicated rows.
  • Rows = rows of query 1 + rows of query 2, exactly.
  • Use it when duplicates are meaningful (every occurrence, totals) or when you know there are none (faster: no duplicate check).

Exam wording: UNION ALL combines the results of two queries without removing duplicated records.
cards.zh:
直觉：UNION 会小心去掉重复；UNION ALL 只是把两张名单钉在一起，较快，全部保留。

  • UNION ALL 保留重复行。
  • 行数 = 两边行数相加。
  • 重复有意义（每次出现、计总数）或肯定没有重复时使用。

要背：UNION ALL combines the results of two queries without removing duplicated records.

ex.q: List every occurrence of each bib number in football and relay, sorted (Example 3.4(a)).
ex.a:
1. Football bibs: 7, 9, 12, 9. Relay: 3, 7, 12.
  2. Every occurrence → UNION ALL; ORDER BY BIB at the end.
  3. 3, 7, 7, 9, 9, 12, 12 (7 rows).
ex.az:
1. 两项的 bib。
  2. UNION ALL 再排序。
  3. 7 行。

ex.q: How many rows does SELECT SID FROM STUDENT UNION ALL SELECT SID FROM STUDENT2 give?
ex.a:
1. 7 + 4 = 11.
  2. Eva's SID appears twice.
ex.az:
1. 7 + 4 = 11。
  2. Eva 出现两次。

ex.q: To count how many different people are in either event, a student uses COUNT on a UNION ALL. Why wrong?
ex.a:
1. Kit and Mei are in both events → counted twice.
  2. UNION ALL keeps duplicates.
  3. Use UNION (distinct people) before counting.
ex.az:
1. Kit、Mei 两项都参加，被数两次。
  2. UNION ALL 保留重复。
  3. 要用 UNION。

demo.query:
SELECT BIB FROM FOOTBALL
UNION ALL
SELECT BIB FROM RELAYRACE
ORDER BY BIB;
demo.note: Every occurrence is kept: 7, 9 and 12 appear twice. Change to UNION to compare.

cards.en:
Intuition: "who is on both lists?" The overlap of two circles.

SELECT PID FROM FOOTBALL
INTERSECT
SELECT PID FROM RELAYRACE
  • Returns rows that appear in both results (duplicates removed).
  • Same column rules as UNION.
  • MySQL supports INTERSECT only from 8.0.31; otherwise use IN with a subquery: WHERE PID IN (SELECT PID FROM RELAYRACE).

Exam wording: INTERSECT returns the records that exist in the results of both queries.
cards.zh:
直觉：“谁两张名单都有？”两个圆的重叠部分。

  • 返回两边结果都有的行（去重）。
  • 字段规则同 UNION。
  • 旧版 MySQL 没有 INTERSECT，可用 IN 子查询代替。

要背：INTERSECT returns the records that exist in the results of both queries.

ex.q: Which participants joined both events?
ex.a:
1. Football PIDs: 1, 2, 3, 5. Relay: 1, 4, 3.
  2. Common: 1, 3.
  3. Kit, Mei.
ex.az:
1. 足球 1,2,3,5；接力 1,4,3。
  2. 共同 1、3。
  3. Kit、Mei。

ex.q: Rewrite without INTERSECT.
ex.a:
1. SELECT PID FROM FOOTBALL WHERE PID IN (SELECT PID FROM RELAYRACE).
  2. Same result: 1, 3.
ex.az:
1. 用 IN 子查询。
  2. 结果相同。

ex.q: 'Participants in team A in at least one event' — a student uses INTERSECT. Correct?
ex.a:
1. 'At least one' = in football-A or relay-A → UNION.
  2. INTERSECT means in both → only people in team A in both (nobody here).
  3. Use UNION.
ex.az:
1. “至少一项” = 或 → UNION。
  2. INTERSECT 是两项都要。
  3. 应用 UNION。

demo.query:
SELECT NAME FROM PARTICIPANT WHERE ID IN (
  SELECT PID FROM FOOTBALL
  INTERSECT
  SELECT PID FROM RELAYRACE);
demo.note: PIDs in both events: 1 and 3 → Kit, Mei.

cards.en:
Intuition: "on list A but not on list B". Take A, cross out anyone in B.

SELECT PID FROM FOOTBALL
EXCEPT
SELECT PID FROM RELAYRACE
  • Returns rows in the first result that are not in the second (duplicates removed).
  • Order matters: A EXCEPT B ≠ B EXCEPT A.
  • Called MINUS in Oracle. Without it, use NOT IN.

Exam wording: EXCEPT returns the records in the result of the first query that do not exist in the result of the second query.
cards.zh:
直觉：“在名单 A 但不在名单 B”：拿 A，划掉 B 有的人。

  • 返回第一个结果中不在第二个结果的行。
  • 次序重要：A EXCEPT B ≠ B EXCEPT A。
  • Oracle 叫 MINUS；没有时用 NOT IN。

要背：EXCEPT returns the records in the result of the first query that do not exist in the result of the second query.

ex.q: Female participants in football but not relay (Example 3.4(c)).
ex.a:
1. Football EXCEPT relay: {1,2,3,5} − {1,3,4} = {2, 5}.
  2. Inside a subquery: WHERE GENDER = 'F' AND ID IN (…).
  3. Lok is male → result Oli.

ex.q: What is RELAYRACE EXCEPT FOOTBALL (PIDs)?
ex.a:
1. {1,3,4} − {1,2,3,5} = {4}.
  2. Nic. (Different from the other order.)
ex.az:
1. 结果 {4}。
  2. Nic，次序不同结果不同。

ex.q: 'Age at least 22 and not in both events at the same time' (Example 3.4(d)). A student uses NOT IN (FOOTBALL UNION RELAYRACE). Wrong?
ex.a:
1. 'Not in both at the same time' excludes only people in both → NOT IN (… INTERSECT …).
  2. NOT IN (UNION) excludes anyone in any event — a different meaning.
  3. Correct: Lok, Oli, Pat (Mei is in both).
ex.az:
1. 只排除两项都参加的人 → INTERSECT。
  2. UNION 会排除参加任何一项的人。
  3. 正确答案 Lok、Oli、Pat。

demo.query:
SELECT NAME FROM PARTICIPANT
WHERE GENDER = 'F' AND ID IN (
  SELECT PID FROM FOOTBALL
  EXCEPT
  SELECT PID FROM RELAYRACE);
demo.note: Football only = {2, 5}; female → Oli.

code.src:
SELECT NAME FROM PARTICIPANT
WHERE AGE >= 22 AND ID NOT IN (
  SELECT PID FROM FOOTBALL
  INTERSECT
  SELECT PID FROM RELAYRACE);

notes.t: Show participant names.
Age at least 22, and ID not in the list below.
People in football …
… who are ALSO …
… in the relay race (in both).

code.out:
NAME
----
Lok
Oli
Pat

cards.t: Summary of the four set operators
cards.en:
Intuition: two circles A and B.

OperatorResultDuplicates
UNIONA or B (everything)removed
UNION ALLA then Bkept
INTERSECTin A and Bremoved
EXCEPTin A, not in Bremoved

Key words in questions: "either / at least one" → UNION; "every occurrence" → UNION ALL; "both" → INTERSECT; "but not" → EXCEPT.

Exam wording: All set operators require the queries to have the same number of fields with compatible data types.
cards.zh:
直觉：两个圆 A、B。

运算结果重复
UNIONA 或 B去除
UNION ALLA 接 B保留
INTERSECTA 且 B去除
EXCEPTA 非 B去除

题目关键词：either/at least one → UNION；every occurrence → UNION ALL；both → INTERSECT；but not → EXCEPT。

要背：All set operators require the queries to have the same number of fields with compatible data types.

ex.q: A = {1,2,3,5}, B = {1,3,4}. Give UNION, INTERSECT, A EXCEPT B, and the row count of UNION ALL.
ex.a:
1. UNION {1,2,3,4,5}.
  2. INTERSECT {1,3}.
  3. A EXCEPT B {2,5}.
  4. UNION ALL: 4 + 3 = 7 rows.
ex.az:
1. UNION 5 个。
  2. INTERSECT 2 个。
  3. EXCEPT {2,5}。
  4. UNION ALL 7 行。

ex.q: 'Participants who joined neither event.'
ex.a:
1. People in either event: FOOTBALL UNION RELAYRACE → {1,2,3,4,5}.
  2. Everyone NOT IN that → Pat.
  3. Or: SELECT ID FROM PARTICIPANT EXCEPT (that union).
ex.az:
1. 先 UNION。
  2. NOT IN → Pat。
  3. 也可用 EXCEPT。

ex.q: A student says INTERSECT keeps duplicates like UNION ALL. True?
ex.a:
1. No: INTERSECT (like UNION and EXCEPT) removes duplicates.
  2. Only UNION ALL keeps them.
ex.az:
1. 错：INTERSECT 会去重。
  2. 只有 UNION ALL 保留。

demo.query:
SELECT NAME FROM PARTICIPANT WHERE ID NOT IN (
  SELECT PID FROM FOOTBALL
  UNION
  SELECT PID FROM RELAYRACE);
demo.note: Everyone in either event is removed → Pat.

cards.t: Enrichment: selecting data from results; several set operators
cards.tz: 增润：从结果中再查询；多个集合运算
cards.en:
Intuition: a combined result is just a table without a name. Give it a name (alias) and you can query it again.

SELECT COUNT(*) FROM
  (SELECT SID FROM STUDENT UNION SELECT SID FROM STUDENT2) u
  • The bracketed query in FROM is a derived table; u is its alias (MySQL requires one).
  • ✗ SELECT COUNT(SID) FROM STUDENT UNION SELECT COUNT(SID) FROM STUDENT2 gives two rows (7 and 4), not one total.
  • Several operators can be chained: A UNION B EXCEPT C (SQLite evaluates left to right).

Exam wording: A combined result can be treated as a table by giving it an alias, so that data can be selected from it.
cards.zh:
直觉：合并结果就是一个没有名字的表，给它一个别名就可以再查询。

  • FROM 里括号中的查询叫 derived table，u 是别名（MySQL 必须有）。
  • ✗ 两个 COUNT 用 UNION 连接 → 得两行（7 和 4），不是总数。
  • 可以连用多个运算：A UNION B EXCEPT C（SQLite 由左至右）。

要背：A combined result can be treated as a table by giving it an alias, so that data can be selected from it.

ex.q: How many different SIDs are in STUDENT and STUDENT2 together?
ex.a:
1. Inner UNION → 10 different SIDs.
  2. Outer COUNT(*) → 10.
ex.az:
1. UNION → 10 个。
  2. COUNT → 10。

ex.q: ISBNs sold in store HBS or WBS but missing in BOOK (Checkpoint 3.4(d)).
ex.a:
1. SELECT ISBN FROM HBS UNION SELECT ISBN FROM WBS → all sold ISBNs.
  2. EXCEPT SELECT ISBN FROM BOOK → remove known books.
  3. Read left to right.
ex.az:
1. 先 UNION。
  2. 再 EXCEPT BOOK。
  3. 由左至右。

ex.q: A student counts with SELECT COUNT(SID) FROM STUDENT UNION SELECT COUNT(SID) FROM STUDENT2 and reports '7'. What's wrong?
ex.a:
1. Each SELECT counts its own table: 7 and 4 → two rows.
  2. Also Eva is in both, so even 7 + 4 = 11 double-counts her.
  3. Count from the derived table → 10.
ex.az:
1. 两个 COUNT → 两行。
  2. 相加 11 也重复计算 Eva。
  3. 应从 derived table 计数 → 10。

demo.query:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS TOTAL FROM
  (SELECT SID FROM STUDENT
   UNION
   SELECT SID FROM STUDENT2) u;
demo.note: The UNION result is named u, then counted: 10.

cards.en:
PARTICIPANT(ID, NAME, GENDER, AGE), FOOTBALL(ID, PID, BIB, TEAM), RELAYRACE(ID, PID, BIB, TEAM). Some people joined no event.

  1. Every occurrence of each bib, sorted → UNION ALL + ORDER BY at end.
  2. In team 'A' in at least one event → UNION, with WHERE TEAM = 'A' in each SELECT.
  3. Female, football but not relay → EXCEPT inside a subquery.
  4. Age ≥ 22 and not in both events at the same time → NOT IN (… INTERSECT …).

Reading tip: "not in both at the same time" ≠ "not in any event".

Exam wording: Choose the set operator by the meaning: either → UNION, both → INTERSECT, only the first → EXCEPT, every occurrence → UNION ALL.
cards.zh:
四个小题：① 每次出现的 bib → UNION ALL；② 至少一项在 A 队 → UNION，两边都写 WHERE；③ 女性、足球但非接力 → 子查询中 EXCEPT；④ ≥ 22 岁且不是两项都参加 → NOT IN (INTERSECT)。

阅读技巧：“不是同时参加两项” ≠ “没有参加任何一项”。

要背：Choose the set operator by meaning: either → UNION, both → INTERSECT, only the first → EXCEPT, every occurrence → UNION ALL.

ex.q: (b) PIDs in team A in at least one event.
ex.a:
1. Football A: 1, 3, 5. Relay A: 4.
  2. UNION → 1, 3, 4, 5.
  3. Kit, Mei, Nic, Oli.
ex.az:
1. 足球 A 1,3,5；接力 A 4。
  2. UNION。
  3. 4 人。

ex.q: (d) Age ≥ 22 and not in both events.
ex.a:
1. Both: {1, 3} (Kit 21, Mei 24).
  2. Age ≥ 22: Lok 23, Mei 24, Oli 22, Pat 25.
  3. Remove Mei → Lok, Oli, Pat.
ex.az:
1. 两项都有 {1,3}。
  2. ≥ 22 岁 4 人。
  3. 去掉 Mei。

ex.q: For (b) a student writes WHERE TEAM = 'A' only after the second SELECT. What's wrong?
ex.a:
1. That WHERE applies only to RELAYRACE.
  2. All football players (team B too, e.g. Lok) are included.
  3. Write WHERE TEAM = 'A' in both SELECTs.
ex.az:
1. WHERE 只作用于接力。
  2. 足球 B 队 Lok 也被包括。
  3. 两边都写。

demo.note: Each SELECT has its own WHERE.

cards.en:
Intuition: a view is a saved question, like a playlist. The songs (data) stay in the library (tables); the playlist only remembers which songs to show. Every time you open it, it shows the current songs.

  • A view is a virtual table defined by a SELECT statement.
  • It stores no data itself; the data come from the base tables each time the view is used.
  • You query it like a table: SELECT … FROM viewname.

Why: the same long join/formula (e.g. final score = SCORE1×0.4 + SCORE2×0.6, joined with CLASS) is written again and again. Put it in a view once, then every task becomes short.

Exam wording: A view is a virtual table based on the result of a SELECT statement. It does not store data, and it simplifies SQL statements for frequently retrieved data.
cards.zh:
直觉：view 是一条保存好的查询，像播放清单：歌曲（数据）仍在曲库（表）里，清单只记住要显示哪些。每次打开都显示最新内容。

  • view 是由 SELECT 定义的虚拟表。
  • 本身不储存数据，每次使用时从 base tables 取。
  • 可以像表一样查询。

用途：同一段长的连接和公式要反复写，放进 view 后每题都变短。

要背：A view is a virtual table based on the result of a SELECT statement. It does not store data, and it simplifies SQL statements for frequently retrieved data.

ex.q: Without a view: names of Mr Suen's students with final score below 60.
ex.a:
1. Join STUDENT and CLASS on CLASS.
  2. WHERE TEACH = 'Mr Suen' AND SCORE1*0.4 + SCORE2*0.6 < 60.
  3. Dio: 58×0.4 + 55×0.6 = 23.2 + 33 = 56.2 → listed.
ex.az:
1. 连接 STUDENT 与 CLASS。
  2. 条件里写公式。
  3. Dio 56.2。

ex.q: Same task with view SCORESHEET (has NAME, TEACH, FSCORE).
ex.a:
1. SELECT NAME FROM SCORESHEET WHERE TEACH = 'Mr Suen' AND FSCORE < 60.
  2. No join, no formula → much shorter.
  3. Result: Dio.
ex.az:
1. 直接查 view。
  2. 不用连接和公式。
  3. Dio。

ex.q: A student says 'a view is a copy of the data, so it uses as much storage as the tables'. Correct?
ex.a:
1. A view stores only its definition (the SELECT statement).
  2. Data are read from the base tables when needed.
  3. So it takes almost no storage. The claim is wrong.
ex.az:
1. view 只储存定义。
  2. 数据用时才从表读取。
  3. 几乎不占空间。

demo.query:
SELECT NAME, FSCORE FROM SCORESHEET
WHERE TEACH = 'Mr Suen' AND FSCORE < 60;
demo.note: SCORESHEET hides the join and the formula. The query is one short line.

cards.en:
Syntax:

CREATE VIEW SCORESHEET AS
  SELECT s.SID, NAME, s.CLASS, TEACH,
         SCORE1*0.4 + SCORE2*0.6 AS FSCORE
  FROM STUDENT s, CLASS cl
  WHERE s.CLASS = cl.CLASS
  • CREATE VIEW name AS + any SELECT (joins, calculations, GROUP BY…).
  • Give calculated columns an alias (FSCORE) so the view has a usable field name.
  • Column names in a view must be unique (alias duplicate names like two NAME fields).
  • After creation, use it like a table: SELECT NAME FROM SCORESHEET WHERE FSCORE > 60.

Exam wording: CREATE VIEW view_name AS SELECT … creates a view; calculated fields should be given aliases.
cards.zh:
语法：CREATE VIEW 名称 AS + 任何 SELECT。

  • 计算字段要用别名（FSCORE），否则 view 中的字段名很难用。
  • view 的字段名不能重复（两个 NAME 要改名）。
  • 建立后像表一样查询。

要背：CREATE VIEW view_name AS SELECT … creates a view; calculated fields should be given aliases.

ex.q: Create view FINAL showing SID, NAME and final score FSCORE.
ex.a:
1. CREATE VIEW FINAL AS SELECT SID, NAME, SCORE1*0.4 + SCORE2*0.6 AS FSCORE FROM STUDENT.
  2. Test: SELECT * FROM FINAL → Clem 89.2 highest.
ex.az:
1. 建立 view。
  2. 测试查询。

ex.q: Using FINAL, list students with FSCORE above 60, highest first.
ex.a:
1. SELECT NAME, FSCORE FROM FINAL WHERE FSCORE > 60 ORDER BY FSCORE DESC.
  2. Clem 89.2, Ben 78.6, Eva 68.4, Ada 66.4.
ex.az:
1. 对 view 查询。
  2. 4 人。

ex.q: A student creates the view without the alias: SELECT NAME, SCORE1*0.4+SCORE2*0.6 FROM STUDENT. Then writes WHERE FSCORE > 60. Result?
ex.a:
1. The column is named 'SCORE1*0.4+SCORE2*0.6', not FSCORE.
  2. → error: no such column FSCORE.
  3. Add AS FSCORE in the view.
ex.az:
1. 字段名变成整条公式。
  2. 找不到 FSCORE → 出错。
  3. 加 AS FSCORE。

demo.note: Create the view once, then query it like a table.

notes.t: Create a view named FINAL defined by the query below.
notes.tz: 建立名为 FINAL 的 view。

notes.t: Fields: SID and NAME …
… plus the calculated final score, alias FSCORE.
Data come from STUDENT.
Use the view like a table.
Filter on the view's alias column.

code.out:
NAME  FSCORE
----  ------
Ada   66.4
Clem  89.2
Eva   68.4
Ben   78.6

cards.tz: 增润：对聚合结果再聚合
cards.en:
Intuition: "the most clubs anyone joins" needs two steps: count per student, then take the max of those counts.

  • ✗ SELECT MAX(COUNT(*)) FROM SC GROUP BY SID → error: an aggregate function cannot be applied directly to another aggregate.
  • Method 1: derived table: SELECT MAX(TOTAL) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS TOTAL FROM SC GROUP BY SID) t
  • Method 2: … GROUP BY SID ORDER BY TOTAL DESC LIMIT 1 (but this shows only one row if there is a tie).
  • Method 3 (simplest): create a view of the counts, then SELECT MAX(CLUBNUM) FROM COUNTCLUB.

Exam wording: An aggregate function cannot summarise the result of another aggregate function directly; treat the aggregated result as a table (or a view) first.
cards.zh:
直觉：“参加最多学会的数目”要两步：先数每个学生，再取最大值。

  • ✗ MAX(COUNT(*)) → 出错。
  • 方法 1：derived table 加别名。
  • 方法 2：ORDER BY … LIMIT 1（同分只显示一行）。
  • 方法 3（最简单）：先建 view，再 MAX。

要背：An aggregate function cannot summarise the result of another aggregate function directly; treat the aggregated result as a table (or a view) first.

ex.q: Find the largest number of clubs joined by one student.
ex.a:
1. Inner: COUNT(*) per SID → Ada 1, Clem 3, Eva 2, Finn 1, Ben 1.
  2. Outer: MAX → 3.
ex.az:
1. 每人计数。
  2. 最大 3。

ex.q: Name(s) of student(s) who join the most clubs.
ex.a:
1. Using view COUNTCLUB: WHERE CLUBNUM = (SELECT MAX(CLUBNUM) FROM COUNTCLUB).
  2. Join with STUDENT for the name → Clem.
ex.az:
1. 用 view 和子查询。
  2. Clem。

ex.q: A student uses ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1 to find all top students. When does it fail?
ex.a:
1. LIMIT 1 always returns one row.
  2. If two students tie for the most clubs, one is missed.
  3. Compare with MAX instead.
ex.az:
1. LIMIT 1 只得一行。
  2. 同分时会漏人。
  3. 应与 MAX 比较。

demo.query:
SELECT MAX(TOTAL) AS MOST FROM
  (SELECT COUNT(*) AS TOTAL FROM SC GROUP BY SID) t;
demo.note: Inner query counts per student; the outer query takes the max.

cards.t: A view does not store data: no manual updates
cards.tz: 视图不储存数据：不用手动更新
cards.en:
Intuition: a playlist updates itself when a song in the library changes. A screenshot of the playlist does not.

  • Because a view refers to the base tables, any change in the tables shows up immediately the next time the view is queried. No manual updates needed.
  • Compare: copying a query result into a new table (CREATE TABLE … AS SELECT) makes a snapshot. It goes out of date → data inconsistency, and it uses extra storage.

Exam wording: A view refers to data from other tables or views, thus does not need manual updates.
cards.zh:
直觉：播放清单会随曲库自动更新；清单的截图却不会。

  • view 引用 base tables，表一改，下次查询 view 就立即反映，不用手动更新。
  • 对比：把结果复制成新表是快照，会过时 → data inconsistency，又多占空间。

要背：A view refers to data from other tables or views, thus does not need manual updates.

ex.q: Finn's SCORE2 changes from 48 to 90. What does view FINAL show for Finn next time?
ex.a:
1. FINAL recalculates from STUDENT each time.
  2. 50×0.4 + 90×0.6 = 20 + 54 = 74.
  3. No UPDATE on the view needed.
ex.az:
1. view 每次重新计算。
  2. 74。
  3. 不用更新 view。

ex.q: A manager copies a join result into table SUMMARY every night. Give two disadvantages vs a view.
ex.a:
1. SUMMARY is out of date between copies → inconsistent data.
  2. It takes extra storage for duplicated data.
  3. (Also: someone must remember to refresh it.)
ex.az:
1. 会过时。
  2. 多占空间。
  3. 要人手更新。

ex.q: A student tries UPDATE FINAL SET FSCORE = 70 WHERE NAME = 'Finn'. What happens?
ex.a:
1. FSCORE is calculated, not stored; there is nothing to update.
  2. SQLite: error (cannot modify a view). Other DBMS reject updates to calculated columns.
  3. Update the base table (SCORE1/SCORE2) instead.
ex.az:
1. FSCORE 是计算出来的。
  2. 出错。
  3. 应更新 STUDENT。

demo.note: We only updated STUDENT. The view already shows Finn's new FSCORE (74).

cards.t: Views can miss records: COUNTCLUB and Dio
cards.tz: 视图可能漏记录：COUNTCLUB 与 Dio
cards.en:
Intuition: if you build the "club count" list from the sign-up sheet only, students who never signed up are not on the list at all, not even with 0.

CREATE VIEW COUNTCLUB AS
  SELECT SID, COUNT(*) AS CLUBNUM FROM SC GROUP BY SID
  • Dio joins no club → no row in SC → not in the view.
  • "Students with no more than 2 clubs" (CLUBNUM <= 2) wrongly misses Dio.
  • Fix: build from STUDENT with a LEFT JOIN and count a field from SC:
SELECT s.SID, COUNT(CID) AS CLUBNUM
FROM STUDENT s LEFT JOIN SC ON SC.SID = s.SID
GROUP BY s.SID

COUNT(CID) (not COUNT(*)) so Dio gets 0, not 1.

Exam wording: A view built only from the linking table misses records with no match; use an outer join from the main table and count a field that is NULL for unmatched records.
cards.zh:
直觉：只用报名表做“学会数目”清单，没报名的学生根本不在清单上，连 0 也没有。

  • Dio 没有学会 → SC 没有他 → view 里也没有。
  • “不多于 2 个学会”会漏掉 Dio。
  • 修正：从 STUDENT LEFT JOIN SC，并用 COUNT(CID)，Dio 得 0 而不是 1。

要背：A view built only from the linking table misses records with no match; use an outer join from the main table and count a field that is NULL for unmatched records.

ex.q: With the SC-only view, who has CLUBNUM <= 2?
ex.a:
1. View rows: Ada 1, Clem 3, Eva 2, Finn 1, Ben 1.
  2. <= 2 → Ada, Eva, Finn, Ben.
  3. Dio is missing!
ex.az:
1. view 只有 5 人。
  2. 4 人符合。
  3. Dio 漏了。

ex.q: Build the fixed view and give Dio's CLUBNUM.
ex.a:
1. STUDENT s LEFT JOIN SC → Dio has one row with CID NULL.
  2. COUNT(CID) ignores NULL → 0.
  3. Now Dio appears for CLUBNUM <= 2.
ex.az:
1. LEFT JOIN。
  2. COUNT(CID) → 0。
  3. Dio 出现。

ex.q: Using the SC-only view, which students satisfy CLUBNUM = 0?
ex.a:
1. Students with no club are not in the view at all.
  2. No row can have CLUBNUM = 0.
  3. Empty result. Need the LEFT JOIN version.
ex.az:
1. 没有学会的人不在 view 中。
  2. 不会有 0。
  3. 结果为空。

demo.query:
SELECT s.NAME, cc.CLUBNUM
FROM STUDENT s LEFT JOIN COUNTCLUB cc ON s.SID = cc.SID;
demo.note: Dio's CLUBNUM is NULL: he is not in the view at all.

cards.t: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW and views built on views
cards.tz: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW 及以视图建视图
cards.en:
Intuition: like editing a saved playlist instead of making a new one with a new name.

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW COUNTCLUB AS
  SELECT s.SID, COUNT(CID) AS CLUBNUM
  FROM STUDENT s LEFT JOIN SC ON SC.SID = s.SID
  GROUP BY s.SID
  • CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW changes an existing view's definition (MySQL). SQLite has no such command: use DROP VIEW then CREATE VIEW.
  • A view can be built on another view: SCORESHEET can join STUDENT, CLASS and COUNTCLUB.
  • Then tasks become one line: SELECT NAME FROM SCORESHEET WHERE FSCORE > 60 AND CLUBNUM >= 2.

Exam wording: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW modifies the structure of an existing view; a view can refer to other views.
cards.zh:
直觉：就像编辑已保存的播放清单，而不是另起一个新名字。

  • CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW 修改现有 view（MySQL）。SQLite 没有，要先 DROP VIEW 再 CREATE VIEW。
  • view 可以建立在另一个 view 上。
  • 之后题目只需一行。

要背：CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW modifies the structure of an existing view; a view can refer to other views.

ex.q: Using SCORESHEET, names with FSCORE above 60 and at least 2 clubs.
ex.a:
1. FSCORE > 60: Ada 66.4, Clem 89.2, Eva 68.4, Ben 78.6.
  2. CLUBNUM >= 2: Clem 3, Eva 2.
  3. Clem, Eva.
ex.az:
1. 总分 > 60 四人。
  2. 学会 ≥ 2：Clem、Eva。
  3. 结果两人。

ex.q: Who joins the most clubs, using SCORESHEET?
ex.a:
1. SELECT NAME FROM SCORESHEET WHERE CLUBNUM = (SELECT MAX(CLUBNUM) FROM SCORESHEET).
  2. MAX = 3 → Clem.
ex.az:
1. 与 MAX 比较。
  2. Clem。

ex.q: In SQLite a student runs CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW. What happens and what should they do?
ex.a:
1. SQLite does not support CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW → syntax error.
  2. Run DROP VIEW COUNTCLUB; then CREATE VIEW COUNTCLUB AS …
  3. (In the DSE exam, MySQL syntax CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW is accepted.)
ex.az:
1. SQLite 不支持 → 出错。
  2. 先 DROP 再 CREATE。
  3. DSE 可用 MySQL 写法。

demo.query:
SELECT NAME, FSCORE, CLUBNUM FROM SCORESHEET
WHERE FSCORE > 60 AND CLUBNUM >= 2;
demo.note: SCORESHEET is built on view COUNTCLUB plus two tables.

notes.t: Remove the old (faulty) view (SQLite way of 'replace').
notes.tz: 删除旧 view（SQLite 的替换方法）。

notes.t: Create it again with the new definition.
Count CID so students without clubs get 0.
Start from STUDENT so every student is kept.
notes.tz: 从 STUDENT 开始，保留所有学生。

notes.t: One row per student.
Now Dio appears with 0.
notes.tz: 现在 Dio 以 0 出现。

cards.en:
Intuition: if playlist B says "play everything in playlist A", deleting A breaks B.

  • DROP VIEW COUNTCLUB deletes a view.
  • Dropping a view never deletes data in the base tables (the view holds none).
  • If view A is used by view B, B no longer works after A is dropped.
  • The same if a table used by a view is dropped.

Exam wording: If the tables or views referred to by a view are deleted, the view no longer works.
cards.zh:
直觉：播放清单 B 写着“播放清单 A 的全部歌”，删掉 A，B 就坏了。

  • DROP VIEW 删除 view。
  • 删除 view 不会删除表中的数据。
  • view B 引用 view A，删 A 后 B 不能再用。
  • 被引用的表被删也一样。

要背：If the tables or views referred to by a view are deleted, the view no longer works.

ex.q: SCORESHEET uses COUNTCLUB. What happens after DROP VIEW COUNTCLUB?
ex.a:
1. SCORESHEET's definition mentions COUNTCLUB.
  2. Querying SCORESHEET now gives an error.
  3. STUDENT, SC, CLASS data are unchanged.
ex.az:
1. SCORESHEET 引用 COUNTCLUB。
  2. 查询会出错。
  3. 表数据不变。

ex.q: View CPAYMENT is built on view FORDER2, which is built on table FORDER. Which views break if FORDER is dropped?
ex.a:
1. FORDER2 refers to FORDER → breaks.
  2. CPAYMENT refers to FORDER2 → also breaks.
  3. Both.
ex.az:
1. FORDER2 坏。
  2. CPAYMENT 也坏。
  3. 两个都坏。

ex.q: A student says 'DROP VIEW SCORESHEET will delete all students' final scores'. Correct?
ex.a:
1. Final scores were never stored; they are calculated from SCORE1 and SCORE2.
  2. Dropping the view only removes the definition.
  3. Data are safe. The claim is wrong.
ex.az:
1. 总分从未储存。
  2. 只删除定义。
  3. 说法错。

demo.query:
DROP VIEW SCORESHEET;
SELECT COUNT(*) AS STUDENTS_STILL_THERE FROM STUDENT;
demo.note: The view is gone, but STUDENT still has all 6 rows.

cards.en:
Memorise these five (Chapter Summary):

  1. It is used to show frequently retrieved data;
  2. When used properly, it may simplify SQL statements;
  3. It refers to data from other tables or views, thus does not need manual updates;
  4. Similar to tables, its structure can be modified (CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW); and
  5. If the referred tables or views are deleted, the view no longer works.

Extra points: a view can hide fields (e.g. show names but not phone numbers) for security; it uses almost no storage; it is always consistent with the base tables.

Exam wording: A view simplifies SQL statements and needs no manual updates because it refers to data in other tables.
cards.zh:
背熟五点：① 用来显示经常取用的数据；② 可简化 SQL；③ 引用其他表/view 的数据，不需手动更新；④ 结构可修改；⑤ 被引用的表/view 删除后，view 不能再用。

额外：可隐藏字段（保安）；几乎不占空间；永远与表一致。

要背：A view simplifies SQL statements and needs no manual updates because it refers to data in other tables.

ex.q: Give two advantages of creating a view SCORESHEET for teachers.
ex.a:
1. Teachers' queries become short: no repeated joins/formulas.
  2. Always up to date with STUDENT, no manual updates.
ex.az:
1. 简化查询。
  2. 自动最新。

ex.q: How can a view protect privacy?
ex.a:
1. Create a view with only NAME and CLASS (no phone, address).
  2. Give users access to the view, not the table.
  3. They cannot see the hidden fields.
ex.az:
1. 只放部分字段。
  2. 只开放 view。
  3. 看不到隐藏字段。

ex.q: A student writes 'A view speeds up searching because the data are sorted.' Correct?
ex.a:
1. That describes an index, not a view.
  2. A view runs its SELECT each time; it does not sort or store data.
  3. View = simplify statements; index = speed up searching.
ex.az:
1. 这是 index 的特性。
  2. view 不排序、不储存。
  3. 要分清。

cards.en:
Intuition: finding "Guy" in an unsorted pile of 1000 forms means checking one by one. A phone book is sorted, so you jump to the middle and halve the search each time.

  • An index is a separate, sorted structure (index table) of the values of a field, each with a pointer to its record.
  • Without an index the DBMS must check records one by one (linear search).
  • With an index it can do binary search: check the middle, throw away half, repeat.
  • Max checks with binary search for n records ≈ the smallest k with 2k ≥ n. 1024 records → 10 checks.

Exam wording: An index allows the DBMS to perform binary search on the indexed field to speed up the data retrieval process.
cards.zh:
直觉：在一叠未排序的 1000 张表格中找 Guy，要逐张看；电话簿是排好序的，可以从中间翻，每次去掉一半。

  • index 是一个独立、已排序的结构（index table），每个值附有指向记录的指针。
  • 没有 index → 逐条检查（linear search）。
  • 有 index → binary search：看中间，丢掉一半，重复。
  • n 条记录最多检查次数 ≈ 最小的 k 使 2k ≥ n；1024 → 10 次。

要背：An index allows the DBMS to perform binary search on the indexed field to speed up the data retrieval process.

ex.q: Search 'Guy' in sorted names: Ada, Ben, Clem, Dio, Eva, Finn, Gabe, Guy, Hans, Ivy, Jean (11).
ex.a:
1. Middle (6th) Finn: F < G → drop 1–6.
  2. Middle of 7–11 (9th) Hans: H > G → drop 9–11.
  3. 7th Gabe: 'Ga' < 'Gu' → drop 7.
  4. 8th Guy: found. 4 checks instead of up to 11.
ex.az:
1. 第 6 个 Finn。
  2. 第 9 个 Hans。
  3. 第 7 个 Gabe。
  4. 第 8 个 Guy，4 次。

ex.q: An indexed field has 2000 records. Max checks with and without the index?
ex.a:
1. 210 = 1024 < 2000 ≤ 2048 = 211.
  2. With index: at most 11.
  3. Without: up to 2000.

ex.q: A student says 'binary search works on any field, index or not.' Correct?
ex.a:
1. Binary search needs the values to be sorted.
  2. Table records are not stored in order of that field.
  3. The index provides the sorted order. Without it, only linear search is possible.
ex.az:
1. binary search 需要已排序。
  2. 表本身未按该字段排序。
  3. 要靠 index。

cards.en:
Intuition: a sorted phone book is great for searching, but every time someone new moves in, the book must be re-sorted. That takes time and paper.

The index table must be updated when:

  • the data in the indexed field changes (Guy renamed Gal);
  • a new record is added (new student Hope) (and when records are deleted).

The DBMS does this automatically, but it still takes time to update and takes storage space.

Rule: index a field only if it is searched frequently. Too many indices slow down INSERT/UPDATE and waste space.

Exam wording: It takes time for the DBMS to update the index and storage space to store it, so only frequently searched fields should be indexed.
cards.zh:
直觉：排好序的电话簿很好查，但每有新住户就要重新排，费时又费纸。

以下情况 index 要更新：被索引字段的数据改变；新增记录（以及删除记录）。DBMS 会自动更新，但需要时间，也占储存空间。

规则：只为经常被搜寻的字段建立 index。

要背：It takes time for the DBMS to update the index and storage space to store it, so only frequently searched fields should be indexed.

ex.q: Table LOG gets 10 000 new rows per minute, searched once a month by USERID. Index USERID?
ex.a:
1. Each insert forces an index update → slows 10 000 inserts per minute.
  2. Index takes storage.
  3. Search is rare → don't index.
ex.az:
1. 每次插入都要更新 index。
  2. 占空间。
  3. 很少查 → 不建。

ex.q: CUSTOMER is searched by PHONE hundreds of times a day, but rarely changes. Index PHONE?
ex.a:
1. Frequent searches benefit from binary search.
  2. Few changes → little update cost.
  3. Yes, index PHONE.
ex.az:
1. 经常查。
  2. 少改。
  3. 应建立。

ex.q: A student says 'index every field, then every query is fast.' What's wrong?
ex.a:
1. Every INSERT/UPDATE must update all those indices → slower changes.
  2. Lots of extra storage.
  3. Only frequently searched fields should be indexed.
ex.az:
1. 每次修改要更新所有 index。
  2. 大量空间。
  3. 只索引常查字段。

cards.en:
Syntax:

CREATE INDEX NAMEIDX ON STUDENT (NAME);
DROP INDEX NAMEIDX;            -- SQLite
DROP INDEX NAMEIDX ON STUDENT; -- MySQL
  • Give the index a name, the table, and the field(s) in brackets.
  • Queries do not change: the DBMS uses the index automatically when it helps (e.g. WHERE NAME = 'Guy').
  • A primary key is normally indexed automatically.
  • Dropping an index removes only the index, not data.

Exam wording: CREATE INDEX index_name ON table_name (field_name) creates an index on a field; DROP INDEX removes it.
cards.zh:
语法：CREATE INDEX 名称 ON 表 (字段)。删除：SQLite 写 DROP INDEX 名称；MySQL 写 DROP INDEX 名称 ON 表。

  • 要写 index 名称、表名、括号内的字段。
  • 查询语句不用改，DBMS 会自动使用 index。
  • primary key 通常自动有 index。
  • 删除 index 不会删除数据。

要背：CREATE INDEX index_name ON table_name (field_name) creates an index on a field; DROP INDEX removes it.

ex.q: Create an index on CLASS of STUDENT.
ex.a:
1. Choose a name: CLASSIDX.
  2. CREATE INDEX CLASSIDX ON STUDENT (CLASS);
ex.az:
1. 取名 CLASSIDX。
  2. 见左边。

ex.q: How do you see whether SQLite uses the index for WHERE NAME = 'Eva'?
ex.a:
1. Run EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN SELECT * FROM STUDENT WHERE NAME = 'Eva'.
  2. Output mentions 'USING INDEX NAMEIDX' → binary search on the index.
  3. Without the index it says 'SCAN STUDENT' (row by row).
ex.az:
1. EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN。
  2. 显示 USING INDEX。
  3. 否则 SCAN。

ex.q: A student writes CREATE INDEX ON STUDENT NAME. Errors?
ex.a:
1. The index name is missing (required in SQLite/MySQL syntax taught).
  2. The field must be in brackets: (NAME).
  3. Correct: CREATE INDEX NAMEIDX ON STUDENT (NAME);
ex.az:
1. 缺 index 名称。
  2. 字段要加括号。
  3. 见正确写法。

demo.query:
CREATE INDEX NAMEIDX ON STUDENT (NAME);
EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN SELECT * FROM STUDENT WHERE NAME = 'Eva';
demo.note: The plan shows SEARCH … USING INDEX NAMEIDX: binary search instead of scanning.

notes.t: Before: plan shows SCAN (check every row).
Create an index called NAMEIDX on field NAME.
notes.tz: 在 NAME 上建立 NAMEIDX。

notes.t: After: plan shows SEARCH using the index.
notes.tz: 之后：使用 index 搜寻。

notes.t: Remove the index (data stay).

ex.q: State one advantage and two disadvantages of indexing PHONE in CUSTOMER.
ex.a:
1. Advantage: searching by PHONE is faster (binary search on the sorted index).
  2. Disadvantage 1: takes storage space.
  3. Disadvantage 2: takes time to update when a phone changes or a customer is added.
ex.az:
1. 优点：搜寻快。
  2. 缺点：占空间。
  3. 缺点：更新费时。

ex.q: View or index? 'Teachers keep writing the same 3-table join.'
ex.a:
1. The problem is long statements, not slow searching.
  2. → View.
ex.az:
1. 问题是语句长。
  2. → view。

ex.q: A student writes 'An index stores no data so it needs no storage.' Correct?
ex.a:
1. That is a property of a view.
  2. An index stores sorted copies of the field values plus pointers → needs storage.
  3. Wrong.
ex.az:
1. 这是 view 的特性。
  2. index 要储存排序值。
  3. 错。

cards.en:
PATIENT(ID, PNAME, SEX, WEIGHT, HEIGHT, RID), ROOM(ID, RNAME, CAPACITY). Not every room has patients; some patients have no room yet.

  • (a) View RPNUM (each room's patient count): ROOM LEFT JOIN PATIENT, GROUP BY r.ID (not RID, which is NULL for empty rooms), COUNT(p.ID) (COUNT(*) would give empty rooms 1).
  • (b) rooms with free beds: SELECT RNAME FROM RPNUM WHERE PNUM < CAPACITY
  • (c) average patients per room except B01: SELECT AVG(PNUM) FROM RPNUM WHERE RNAME <> 'B01'
  • (d) View PBMI: PATIENT LEFT JOIN ROOM, BMI = WEIGHT/HEIGHT/HEIGHT.
  • (e) lowest BMI per sex: GROUP BY SEX on PBMI.

Exam wording: Use LEFT JOIN in the view so that rooms without patients (or patients without rooms) are not missed.
cards.zh:
(a) view RPNUM：ROOM LEFT JOIN PATIENT，按 r.ID 分组，COUNT(p.ID)。(b) 有空床：PNUM < CAPACITY。(c) 除 B01 外平均人数。(d) view PBMI：PATIENT LEFT JOIN ROOM，BMI = WEIGHT/HEIGHT/HEIGHT。(e) 按性别求最低 BMI。

要背：Use LEFT JOIN in the view so that rooms without patients (or patients without rooms) are not missed.

ex.q: (a)+(b) Which rooms have free beds?
ex.a:
1. RPNUM: A01 2 patients (cap 2), B01 1 (cap 3), C01 0 (cap 2).
  2. PNUM < CAPACITY → B01, C01.
ex.az:
1. 每间人数。
  2. B01、C01。

ex.q: Leo weighs 72 kg, height 1.8 m. BMI in PBMI?
ex.a:
1. 72 / 1.8 = 40; 40 / 1.8 = 22.2.
  2. Dividing by HEIGHT twice = dividing by HEIGHT².

ex.q: A student builds RPNUM with COUNT(*) and GROUP BY RID. What goes wrong for C01?
ex.a:
1. C01 has no patient → RID is NULL in its row → GROUP BY RID loses its identity.
  2. COUNT(*) counts the NULL row → C01 = 1 (wrong).
  3. Use GROUP BY r.ID and COUNT(p.ID) → 0.
ex.az:
1. 空房 RID 为 NULL。
  2. COUNT(*) 得 1。
  3. 改用 r.ID 和 COUNT(p.ID)。

demo.note: C01 is empty but still listed with PNUM 0.

notes.t: Create view PBMI.
Patient ID, name and sex.
BMI = weight ÷ height ÷ height, rounded to 1 d.p.
Keep patients without a room (Ned).
(e) Lowest BMI for each sex.

cards.t: Checkpoint 3.5 pattern: views of views for payments
cards.tz: Checkpoint 3.5 模式：用视图的视图计算付款
cards.en:
Food delivery: CUSTOMER(CID, CNAME, SEX, DEPOSIT), MEAL(MID, MNAME, OPRICE, DISCOUNT), FORDER(CID, MID, NUM, ETA, PAID).

  • FORDER2 (view): unpaid orders with total price OPRICE*(1-DISCOUNT)*NUM AS TPRICE.
  • CPAYMENT (view on a view): amount due per customer, keeping customers with no unpaid order:
    CREATE VIEW CPAYMENT AS
  SELECT CNAME, SEX, DEPOSIT, SUM(TPRICE) AS DUE
  FROM CUSTOMER c LEFT JOIN FORDER2 f ON c.CID = f.CID
  GROUP BY c.CID
  • Customers whose deposit is not enough: SELECT CNAME FROM CPAYMENT WHERE DEPOSIT < DUE.
  • No unpaid order → DUE is NULL; DEPOSIT < NULL is not TRUE, so they are correctly not listed.

Exam wording: A view can refer to another view, so complex calculations can be built up step by step.
cards.zh:
外卖例子：FORDER2 是未付款订单及总价的 view；CPAYMENT 建在 FORDER2 上，计算每位顾客应付金额，用 LEFT JOIN 保留没有欠款的顾客。按金不足：DEPOSIT < DUE。没有欠款时 DUE 为 NULL，比较不成立，所以不会被列出。

要背：A view can refer to another view, so complex calculations can be built up step by step.

ex.q: Amy: 2 Curry ($40, 25% off) and 1 Noodles ($30), both unpaid. DUE? Listed if deposit is $100?
ex.a:
1. Curry: 40 × 0.75 × 2 = 60.
  2. Noodles: 30 × 1 × 1 = 30.
  3. DUE = 90; 100 < 90 is false → not listed.

ex.q: Bill: 3 Curry unpaid, deposit $50. Listed?
ex.az:
1. 90。
  2. 列出。

ex.q: A student builds CPAYMENT with FORDER2 INNER JOIN CUSTOMER. What happens to Cora (all paid)?
ex.a:
1. Cora has no row in FORDER2 → dropped by INNER JOIN.
  2. The question wants all customers.
  3. Use CUSTOMER LEFT JOIN FORDER2.
ex.az:
1. Cora 在 FORDER2 没有记录。
  2. 被 INNER JOIN 去掉。
  3. 改用 LEFT JOIN。

demo.note: Cora has DUE NULL (all paid). Only Bill cannot cover his orders.

ex.a: 1. 'but not' → EXCEPT.

ex.a: 1. All of CLUB → CLUB LEFT JOIN STUDENT.
ex.az: 1. CLUB LEFT JOIN STUDENT。

  2. > ANY only needs to beat the lowest one.

mc.q: Which of the following is a problem of storing club name, room and teacher inside every student record?
o: A new club with no members cannot be stored if SID is the primary key
mc.e: With club data inside STUDENT, a club without students has no SID, but SID is the primary key and cannot be NULL, so the club cannot be stored (insertion problem).
mc.ez: 主键 SID 不能是 NULL，没有学生的新学会无法储存。

mc.q: Science Club (3 members) moves to Room 301. How many records must be updated if club data is stored in STUDENT, and how many if it is stored in a separate CLUB table?
mc.e: Each member's record holds the room in the single-table design (3 updates); with a CLUB table, only one record changes.
mc.ez: 单表要改 3 条，分表只改 1 条。

mc.q: What is the main advantage of a linking table SC(SID, CID) when students may join many clubs?
o: A student may join many clubs without duplicating student data
It stores the number of clubs of each student
It removes the need for primary keys
mc.e: Each (student, club) pair becomes one row in SC, so student data in STUDENT is never repeated.
mc.ez: 学生可参加多个学会而不重复储存学生资料。

mc.q:
Use the textbook tables STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) (Ada 3A 0 CID 2; Clem 3B 89 CID 1; Eva 3B 83 CID 4; Gabe 3C 47 CID 4; Finn 3B 35 CID 1; Dio 3C 67 CID 4; Ben 3A 86 CID NULL; clubs 1 Chess, 2 Art, 3 English, 4 Science). How many rows does the following return?
SELECT * FROM STUDENT INNER JOIN CLUB ON STUDENT.CID = CLUB.CID
mc.e: Only matched records: Ben (NULL) and English Club (no student) are excluded, leaving 6.
mc.ez: 只有配对的记录，共 6 行。

mc.q:
Use the textbook tables STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) (Ada 3A 0 CID 2; Clem 3B 89 CID 1; Eva 3B 83 CID 4; Gabe 3C 47 CID 4; Finn 3B 35 CID 1; Dio 3C 67 CID 4; Ben 3A 86 CID NULL; clubs 1 Chess, 2 Art, 3 English, 4 Science). How many rows does the following return?
SELECT * FROM STUDENT LEFT JOIN CLUB ON STUDENT.CID = CLUB.CID
mc.e: All 7 students are kept; Ben gets NULL club fields; English Club is not included.
mc.ez: 保留全部 7 个学生。

mc.q:
Use the textbook tables STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) (Ada 3A 0 CID 2; Clem 3B 89 CID 1; Eva 3B 83 CID 4; Gabe 3C 47 CID 4; Finn 3B 35 CID 1; Dio 3C 67 CID 4; Ben 3A 86 CID NULL; clubs 1 Chess, 2 Art, 3 English, 4 Science). How many rows does the following return?
SELECT * FROM CLUB LEFT JOIN STUDENT ON CLUB.CID = STUDENT.CID
mc.e: All clubs are kept: 6 matched rows plus English Club with NULL student = 7. This equals STUDENT RIGHT JOIN CLUB.
mc.ez: 6 行配对加 English Club 一行，共 7 行。

mc.q: Which statement about FULL JOIN is correct?
o: It is the same as CROSS JOIN
It includes unmatched records from both tables and is not available in MySQL
It requires the two tables to have the same number of fields
mc.e: FULL JOIN keeps records from both the left and right tables; MySQL does not support the keyword (use LEFT JOIN … UNION … RIGHT JOIN).
mc.ez: FULL JOIN 两边都保留；MySQL 不支援此关键字。

mc.q: In MySQL, which can produce the same result as STUDENT FULL JOIN CLUB?
o: The result of STUDENT LEFT JOIN CLUB combined by UNION with the result of STUDENT RIGHT JOIN CLUB
mc.e: LEFT JOIN keeps unmatched students, RIGHT JOIN keeps unmatched clubs, and UNION merges them removing duplicate matched rows.
mc.ez: LEFT JOIN 结果 UNION RIGHT JOIN 结果。

mc.q: Which statement about the ON clause of a LEFT JOIN is correct?
o: ON can only be used with INNER JOIN
ON CLUB.CID = STUDENT.CID gives a different result from ON STUDENT.CID = CLUB.CID
ON must always use fields with the same name
The order of the two fields in ON has no effect; the order of the tables does
mc.e: Which CID comes first in the ON clause has no effect; which table is written first (left table) does.
mc.ez: ON 中字段次序无影响，表的左右次序才有影响。

mc.q:
Use the textbook tables STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) (Ada 3A 0 CID 2; Clem 3B 89 CID 1; Eva 3B 83 CID 4; Gabe 3C 47 CID 4; Finn 3B 35 CID 1; Dio 3C 67 CID 4; Ben 3A 86 CID NULL; clubs 1 Chess, 2 Art, 3 English, 4 Science). Why does the following cause an error?
SELECT NAME, ROOM FROM STUDENT LEFT JOIN CLUB ON STUDENT.CID = CLUB.CID
o: ROOM is not a field of CLUB
NAME is ambiguous because both tables have a field called NAME
LEFT JOIN cannot select specific fields
CID must be written as STUDENT.CID in SELECT
mc.e: Both STUDENT and CLUB have NAME, so the table must be specified (STUDENT.NAME or CLUB.NAME).
mc.ez: 两表都有 NAME，须注明表名。

mc.q:
Use the textbook tables STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) (Ada 3A 0 CID 2; Clem 3B 89 CID 1; Eva 3B 83 CID 4; Gabe 3C 47 CID 4; Finn 3B 35 CID 1; Dio 3C 67 CID 4; Ben 3A 86 CID NULL; clubs 1 Chess, 2 Art, 3 English, 4 Science). What is returned?
SELECT c.NAME FROM STUDENT s INNER JOIN CLUB c ON s.CID = c.CID
WHERE s.SCORE > 80 ORDER BY c.NAME
o: Art Club, Chess Club, Science Club
mc.e: Scores above 80: Clem 89 (Chess), Eva 83 (Science), Ben 86 (no club, dropped by INNER JOIN). Sorted: Chess Club, Science Club.
mc.ez: Ben 没有学会被 INNER JOIN 排除。

mc.q:
Use the textbook tables STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) (Ada 3A 0 CID 2; Clem 3B 89 CID 1; Eva 3B 83 CID 4; Gabe 3C 47 CID 4; Finn 3B 35 CID 1; Dio 3C 67 CID 4; Ben 3A 86 CID NULL; clubs 1 Chess, 2 Art, 3 English, 4 Science). What does the following return for English Club?
SELECT c.NAME, COUNT(*) FROM CLUB c
  LEFT JOIN STUDENT s ON s.CID = c.CID GROUP BY c.CID
mc.e: The LEFT JOIN creates one row (English Club, NULL student). COUNT(*) counts rows, so it gives 1. COUNT(s.SID) would give 0.
mc.ez: COUNT(*) 计算行数，得 1；应用 COUNT(s.SID) 得 0。

mc.q:
Use the textbook tables STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) (Ada 3A 0 CID 2; Clem 3B 89 CID 1; Eva 3B 83 CID 4; Gabe 3C 47 CID 4; Finn 3B 35 CID 1; Dio 3C 67 CID 4; Ben 3A 86 CID NULL; clubs 1 Chess, 2 Art, 3 English, 4 Science). What is the average score shown for Chess Club?
SELECT c.NAME, AVG(SCORE) FROM STUDENT s LEFT JOIN CLUB c ON s.CID = c.CID
WHERE s.SID <> '03506' GROUP BY c.CID HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
mc.e: Chess Club members: Clem 89 and Finn 35, average 62. (Gabe, removed by WHERE, is in Science Club.)

mc.q: A manager wants each team's average salary, excluding teams whose average salary is below 20000. Which clause should contain the condition?
mc.e: The condition is on a group summary, so it must be in HAVING after GROUP BY. WHERE would exclude individual employees before grouping.
mc.ez: 条件针对组的汇总值，要用 HAVING。

mc.q: TEAM stores MEMNUM, the number of employees in each team. Why is this field undesirable?
o: It cannot be a primary key
It takes the place of a foreign key
It must be updated whenever employees are added, or data becomes inconsistent; it can be computed with COUNT()
mc.e: MEMNUM is derivable data. Storing it risks data inconsistency; compute it with COUNT() instead.
mc.ez: 可计算的数据，储存会造成不一致。

mc.q: Every employee belongs to a department. To list each employee with their department name, excluding departments with no employees, which joins are suitable when EMPLOYEE is the left table?
mc.e: No employee lacks a department, so LEFT and INNER give the same result. RIGHT JOIN would add departments with no employees.
mc.ez: LEFT 和 INNER 结果相同；RIGHT 会多出空部门。

mc.q: Which statement is equivalent to STUDENT INNER JOIN CLUB ON STUDENT.CID = CLUB.CID?
o: SELECT * FROM STUDENT CROSS JOIN CLUB
SELECT * FROM STUDENT LEFT JOIN CLUB ON STUDENT.CID = CLUB.CID
SELECT * FROM STUDENT, CLUB WHERE STUDENT.CID = CLUB.CID
mc.e: Equi-join (tables in FROM with an equality condition in WHERE) is another way to perform INNER JOIN.
mc.ez: Equi-join 就是 INNER JOIN 的另一写法。

mc.q: Use the textbook tables STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) (Ada 3A 0 CID 2; Clem 3B 89 CID 1; Eva 3B 83 CID 4; Gabe 3C 47 CID 4; Finn 3B 35 CID 1; Dio 3C 67 CID 4; Ben 3A 86 CID NULL; clubs 1 Chess, 2 Art, 3 English, 4 Science). How many rows does SELECT * FROM STUDENT, CLUB return (no WHERE clause)?
mc.e: Without a join condition, this is a CROSS JOIN: 7 × 4 = 28 rows.
mc.ez: 没有条件即 CROSS JOIN，7 × 4 = 28。

mc.q: Why can't the textbook's STUDENT and CLUB tables be joined properly with NATURAL JOIN?
o: NATURAL JOIN needs an ON clause
They share two field names, NAME and CID, and NAME is not a foreign key
mc.e: NATURAL JOIN joins on all same-named fields; joining on NAME (student name = club name) is meaningless.
mc.ez: 两表有 NAME、CID 两个同名栏位，NAME 不是外键。

mc.q: What is required to perform a self join?
o: The table must have a composite primary key
The same table must be given two different aliases
The table must contain NULL values
The table must be joined with CROSS JOIN
mc.e: Two aliases let the DBMS treat the table as two different tables temporarily.
mc.ez: 同一表要给两个不同别名。

mc.q: STUDENT has CMSID, the SID of each student's class monitor. Which lists each student with their monitor's name?
o: SELECT s1.NAME, s2.NAME FROM STUDENT s1 INNER JOIN STUDENT s2 ON s1.SID = s2.SID
SELECT NAME, NAME FROM STUDENT WHERE CMSID = SID
SELECT s1.NAME, s2.NAME FROM STUDENT s1 INNER JOIN STUDENT s2 ON s1.CMSID = s2.SID
mc.e: s1 is the student, s2 the monitor; the link is s1.CMSID = s2.SID.
mc.ez: s1 是学生，s2 是班长，条件 s1.CMSID = s2.SID。

mc.q: When pairing students from STUDENT s1, STUDENT s2, which extra condition removes both self-pairs and duplicated pairs?
mc.e: s1.SID < s2.SID excludes equal SIDs (self-pairs) and keeps only one ordering of each pair. <> alone still leaves duplicates.
mc.ez: < 同时去除自配和重复；<> 仍有重复。

mc.q:
Use the textbook tables STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) (Ada 3A 0 CID 2; Clem 3B 89 CID 1; Eva 3B 83 CID 4; Gabe 3C 47 CID 4; Finn 3B 35 CID 1; Dio 3C 67 CID 4; Ben 3A 86 CID NULL; clubs 1 Chess, 2 Art, 3 English, 4 Science). How many rows are returned?
SELECT s1.NAME, s2.NAME FROM STUDENT s1, STUDENT s2
WHERE ABS(s1.SCORE - s2.SCORE) < 16 AND s1.SID < s2.SID
mc.e: Pairs: Clem–Eva, Clem–Ben, Eva–Ben, Gabe–Finn = 4.
mc.ez: 共 4 对。

mc.q:
Use STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE), SC(SID, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) from the textbook (Clem joins clubs 1, 2, 4; Ada 2; Eva 4; Gabe 4; Finn 1; Dio 4; Ben none; English Club (3) has no member). How many rows does the following return?
SELECT s.NAME, c.NAME FROM STUDENT s
  LEFT JOIN SC ON SC.SID = s.SID
  LEFT JOIN CLUB c ON c.CID = SC.CID
mc.e: 8 rows of SC give 8 (student, club) rows, plus Ben with NULL = 9.
mc.ez: SC 8 行加 Ben 一行，共 9 行。

mc.q:
Use STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE), SC(SID, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) from the textbook (Clem joins clubs 1, 2, 4; Ada 2; Eva 4; Gabe 4; Finn 1; Dio 4; Ben none; English Club (3) has no member). How many rows does the equi-join version return?
SELECT s.NAME, c.NAME FROM STUDENT s, SC, CLUB c
WHERE SC.SID = s.SID AND c.CID = SC.CID
mc.e: Equi-join is an INNER JOIN, so Ben (no club) is dropped: 8 rows.
mc.ez: Ben 被排除，8 行。

mc.q: What does GROUP_CONCAT(c.NAME) do in a query grouped by student?
o: Counts the clubs of each student
Joins the club names of each group into one comma-separated string
mc.e: GROUP_CONCAT combines multiple string values in a group into one string, so a student's clubs appear in one row.
mc.ez: 把同组字串合并成一个以逗号分隔的字串。

mc.q: In Example 3.2, to list each employee with the name of their team leader using EMPLOYEE and TEAM, what is needed?
o: Two copies of EMPLOYEE with different aliases
mc.e: The leader is also an employee, so EMPLOYEE is used twice (e for members, l for leaders).
mc.ez: 组长也是员工，EMPLOYEE 要用两个别名。

mc.q: Table L has 3 rows and table R has 5 rows. How many rows does L CROSS JOIN R return?
mc.e: CROSS JOIN matches each row of L with each row of R: 3 × 5 = 15.

mc.q: BUYER Ada needs 4 apples and 7 oranges. Seller Finn sells apples at $14.0 and oranges at $11.4. What COST does PA*NA+PO*NO give?
What does SELECT NAME, MAX(SCORE) FROM STUDENT return according to the textbook?
o: The highest score with a name that is not related to it
The name of the top scorer and the top score
mc.e: NAME is not summarised data; it is just the first student's name, unrelated to MAX(SCORE).
mc.ez: NAME 与 MAX(SCORE) 无关。

mc.q:
Use STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE), SC(SID, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) from the textbook (Clem joins clubs 1, 2, 4; Ada 2; Eva 4; Gabe 4; Finn 1; Dio 4; Ben none; English Club (3) has no member). What is returned?
SELECT NAME FROM STUDENT WHERE SCORE > (SELECT AVG(SCORE) FROM STUDENT)
mc.e: Average = 407 / 7 ≈ 58.1. Above it: Clem 89, Eva 83, Dio 67, Ben 86.

mc.q: Why does WHERE SCORE = (SELECT SCORE FROM STUDENT2) cause an error when STUDENT2 has three rows?
o: A subquery after = must return a single value
= must be written as IN for numbers
mc.e: After a comparison operator, the subquery must return one value; use IN for a list.
mc.ez: 比较运算符后的子查询必须只返回一个值。

mc.q:
Use STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE), SC(SID, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) from the textbook (Clem joins clubs 1, 2, 4; Ada 2; Eva 4; Gabe 4; Finn 1; Dio 4; Ben none; English Club (3) has no member). What is returned?
SELECT NAME FROM STUDENT WHERE SID NOT IN (SELECT SID FROM SC)
mc.e: Every student except Ben appears in SC.
mc.ez: 只有 Ben 不在 SC。

mc.q: Which statement about the subquery after IN is correct?
o: It should select only a single field, returning one list of values
It may select any number of fields
It must return exactly one row
mc.e: IN checks a single list of values, so the subquery selects only one field.
mc.ez: IN 后子查询只选一个栏位。

mc.q: The join version SELECT s.NAME FROM STUDENT s, SC WHERE s.SID = SC.SID AND SCORE > 70 lists Clem three times. What fixes this?
mc.e: Clem has three rows in SC; SELECT DISTINCT removes duplicates. The IN version avoids them naturally.
mc.ez: 加 DISTINCT。

mc.q: STUDENT has fields (SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE); STUDENT2 has (ID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, DOB). Which INSERT works?
o: INSERT INTO STUDENT (SELECT ID, NAME FROM STUDENT2)
INSERT INTO STUDENT (SELECT ID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, 0 FROM STUDENT2)
mc.e: The subquery must return the same number of fields as STUDENT (5); names need not match. SELECT * would put DOB into SCORE (wrong meaning).
mc.ez: 栏位数目要相同（5 个），名称不必相同。

mc.q: Which statement best describes EXISTS?
o: It compares a value with all values in a list
It checks whether a value appears in a list
It checks whether a subquery returns at least one row
mc.e: EXISTS checks for the existence of the result of a subquery.
mc.ez: 检查子查询是否有结果。

mc.q: In WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM STUDENT2 s2 WHERE s.SCORE = s2.SCORE), what can replace the 1?
o: Any field or value, since it is not used for comparison or display
mc.e: EXISTS only checks whether rows exist, so the selected value does not matter.
mc.ez: 选什么都可以，EXISTS 只看是否有行。

mc.q: STUDENT2 scores are 83, 47 and NULL. How many rows does SELECT NAME FROM STUDENT WHERE SCORE NOT IN (SELECT SCORE FROM STUDENT2) return (STUDENT scores 0, 89, 83, 47, 35, 67, 86)?
mc.e: Every comparison with NULL gives NULL, so x NOT IN (83, 47, NULL) is never TRUE.
mc.ez: 与 NULL 比较得 NULL，没有行符合。

mc.q:
With the same data (STUDENT2 scores 83, 47, NULL), how many rows does the NOT EXISTS version return?
SELECT NAME FROM STUDENT s WHERE NOT EXISTS
  (SELECT 1 FROM STUDENT2 s2 WHERE s.SCORE = s2.SCORE)
mc.e: Only Eva (83) and Gabe (47) have a match; the other 5 students are returned.
mc.ez: Eva、Gabe 有配对，其余 5 人返回。

mc.q: Which is equivalent to CLASS = ANY (SELECT CLASS FROM STUDENT2)?
o: CLASS NOT IN (SELECT CLASS FROM STUDENT2)
mc.e: = ANY joins equalities with OR, which is exactly IN.
mc.ez: = ANY 等同 IN。

mc.q: Which of the following is NOT valid SQL?
mc.e: ANY and ALL must be followed by a subquery, not a list of values.
mc.ez: ANY/ALL 后面必须是子查询。

mc.q: New students' classes are 3A, 3B, 3B. Which students satisfy CLASS <> ANY (SELECT CLASS FROM STUDENT2)?
mc.e: <> ANY = <> '3A' OR <> '3B'; every class differs from at least one of them, so it is always TRUE.
mc.ez: 总与其中一个不同，全部成立。

mc.q: New students' scores are 83, 47 and 60. SCORE > ANY (SELECT SCORE FROM STUDENT2) is equivalent to:
mc.e: > ANY means higher than at least one, i.e. higher than the minimum (47).
mc.ez: > ANY = > MIN。

mc.q: New students' scores are 83, 47 and 60. Which STUDENT scores (0, 89, 83, 47, 35, 67, 86) satisfy SCORE < ALL (SELECT SCORE FROM STUDENT2)?
mc.e: < ALL means lower than every one, i.e. < 47. 47 itself is not lower.
mc.ez: < ALL = < MIN = < 47。

mc.q: New students' scores are 83, 47 and 60. Which students satisfy BOTH SCORE > ANY (…) AND SCORE < ANY (…)?
mc.e: > ANY means > 47; < ANY means < 83. Only Dio (67) is in between.
mc.ez: 需要 47 < 分数 < 83，只有 Dio 67。

mc.q: Which is equivalent to NOT IN (subquery)?
mc.e: <> ALL joins inequalities with AND, exactly like NOT IN.
mc.ez: NOT IN = <> ALL。

mc.q: When the subquery returns classes 3A and 3B, what does WHERE CLASS = ALL (subquery) return?
o: No rows, because a class cannot equal two different values
mc.e: = ALL = '3A' AND '3B', impossible to fulfil, like WHERE FALSE.
mc.ez: = ALL 永远不成立。

mc.q: In spoken English 'higher than any new student' means higher than all of them. In SQL, SCORE > ANY (…) means:
o: Higher than at least one of them
mc.e: SQL's ANY means SOME: higher than at least one.
mc.ez: ANY 即 SOME：至少高于一个。

mc.q:
Why is the following statement wrong?
SELECT NAME, h.NAME FROM BREED WHERE ID IN
  (SELECT BID FROM CAT, HOTEL h WHERE HID = h.ID AND h.NAME = 'Alpha')
o: IN cannot be used with a join in the subquery
The main query cannot retrieve data (h.NAME) from the subquery
Aliases are not allowed in subqueries
mc.e: h exists only inside the subquery; to output hotel names you must join in the main query.
mc.ez: 主查询不能取子查询的栏位。

mc.q: A query should list hotels that have no Ragdoll cats. Which is correct?
o: ID IN (SELECT HID FROM CAT, BREED b WHERE BID = b.ID AND b.NAME <> 'Ragdoll')
ID NOT IN (SELECT HID FROM CAT, BREED b WHERE BID = b.ID AND b.NAME = 'Ragdoll')
mc.e: Find hotels that do have Ragdolls, then take the others. The <> version lists hotels with any non-Ragdoll cat and misses hotels with no cats.
mc.ez: 先找有 Ragdoll 的酒店，再 NOT IN。

mc.q: What is the purpose of SELECT h.NAME, COUNT(DISTINCT c.BID) FROM HOTEL h LEFT JOIN CAT c ON h.ID = c.HID GROUP BY h.ID?
o: Count the number of different breeds in each hotel, including hotels with none
List hotels with more cats than capacity
Count the cats in each hotel
mc.e: LEFT JOIN keeps every hotel; COUNT(DISTINCT c.BID) counts different breeds; empty hotels get 0.
mc.ez: 计算每间酒店的品种数目。

mc.q: Which describes a correlated subquery?
o: A subquery that uses only constants
A subquery that refers to a field of the outer query and is evaluated for each outer row
mc.e: E.g. (SELECT COUNT(c.ID) FROM CAT c WHERE HID = h.ID) uses h from the outer query.
mc.ez: 引用外层查询的栏位，对外层每行执行一次。

mc.q:
Use STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE), SC(SID, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) from the textbook (Clem joins clubs 1, 2, 4; Ada 2; Eva 4; Gabe 4; Finn 1; Dio 4; Ben none; English Club (3) has no member). What is returned?
SELECT NAME FROM CLUB WHERE CID IN
  (SELECT CID FROM SC GROUP BY CID HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2)
o: Chess Club, Art Club, Science Club
mc.e: SC counts: club 1 → 2, club 2 → 2, club 4 → 4, club 3 → 0. Clubs with ≥ 2: Chess, Art, Science.
mc.ez: 学会 1、2 各 2 人，学会 4 有 4 人。

mc.q: STUDENT has 7 SIDs; STUDENT2 has 4 STUDENTIDs, one of which (03517) is also in STUDENT. How many rows does SELECT SID FROM STUDENT UNION ALL SELECT STUDENTID FROM STUDENT2 return?
mc.e: UNION ALL keeps duplicates: 7 + 4 = 11.
mc.ez: UNION ALL 保留重复，11 行。

mc.q: Same tables. How many rows does SELECT SID, NAME FROM STUDENT UNION SELECT STUDENTID, NAME FROM STUDENT2 return, given 03517 is 'Ben' in STUDENT and 'Benz' in STUDENT2?
mc.e: Only completely identical rows are removed; (03517, Ben) ≠ (03517, Benz), so all 11 rows remain.
mc.ez: 只有完全相同的行才删除，11 行。

mc.q: Same tables. What does SELECT SID, NAME FROM STUDENT INTERSECT SELECT STUDENTID, NAME FROM STUDENT2 return?
mc.e: No row is completely identical in both results.
mc.ez: 没有完全相同的行，空集。

mc.q: What is the requirement for combining two results with UNION?
mc.e: Only the number of fields must match; names may differ (the first result's names are used).
mc.ez: 栏位数目要相同。

mc.q: Where must ORDER BY be placed in a statement using UNION?
o: At the end, applying to the whole combined result
ORDER BY cannot be used with UNION
mc.e: ORDER BY sorts the whole combined result and must be at the end.
mc.ez: 只能放在最后。

mc.q: In SELECT SID FROM STUDENT UNION SELECT STUDENTID FROM STUDENT2 ORDER BY ?, which field name should be used?
o: Either; both work in all DBMS
mc.e: The combined result takes the field names of the first result, so ORDER BY SID.
mc.ez: 采用第一个结果的栏位名 SID。

mc.q: In SELECT SID FROM STUDENT UNION SELECT STUDENTID FROM STUDENT2 WHERE CLASS = '3B', which rows are filtered by the WHERE clause?
mc.e: Each SELECT has its own WHERE; this WHERE belongs to the second SELECT only.
mc.ez: WHERE 只属于第二个 SELECT。

mc.q: Which is a reason to use UNION ALL rather than UNION?
o: To combine results with different numbers of fields
When the number of occurrences matters; it is also faster as it does not search for duplicates
mc.e: UNION ALL keeps duplicates and skips duplicate checking.
mc.ez: 次数重要时用，且较快。

mc.q: STUDENT SIDs: 03493, 03496, 03505, 03506, 03510, 03513, 03517. STUDENT2 STUDENTIDs: 03517, 03518, 03519, 03520. How many rows does SELECT STUDENTID FROM STUDENT2 EXCEPT SELECT SID FROM STUDENT return?
mc.e: Rows in STUDENT2 but not STUDENT: 03518, 03519, 03520.
mc.ez: STUDENT2 有而 STUDENT 没有的 3 个。

mc.q: Which statement correctly lists participants in team 'A' in at least one of FOOTBALL and RELAYRACE?
o: SELECT PID FROM FOOTBALL WHERE TEAM = 'A' UNION SELECT PID FROM RELAYRACE WHERE TEAM = 'A'
(SELECT PID FROM FOOTBALL UNION SELECT PID FROM RELAYRACE) WHERE TEAM = 'A'
SELECT PID FROM FOOTBALL UNION ALL SELECT PID FROM RELAYRACE
SELECT PID FROM FOOTBALL WHERE TEAM = 'A' INTERSECT SELECT PID FROM RELAYRACE WHERE TEAM = 'A'
mc.e: 'At least one' → UNION; each SELECT needs its own WHERE.
mc.ez: 至少一项 → UNION，各自 WHERE。

mc.q: 'List each participant aged at least 22 who does not participate in both events at the same time.' Which subquery is used with NOT IN?
o: SELECT PID FROM FOOTBALL UNION SELECT PID FROM RELAYRACE
SELECT PID FROM FOOTBALL INTERSECT SELECT PID FROM RELAYRACE
SELECT PID FROM FOOTBALL EXCEPT SELECT PID FROM RELAYRACE
SELECT PID FROM FOOTBALL UNION ALL SELECT PID FROM RELAYRACE
mc.e: Exclude those in both events: NOT IN (… INTERSECT …). UNION would exclude anyone in either event.
mc.ez: 排除同时参加两项的人：INTERSECT。

mc.q: What does SELECT COUNT(SID) FROM STUDENT UNION SELECT COUNT(STUDENTID) FROM STUDENT2 return (7 and 4 records)?
mc.e: Each SELECT produces its own count; UNION stacks them. To count unique IDs use COUNT(*) FROM (… UNION …) u.
mc.ez: 得到两行 7 和 4。

mc.q: Which describes joining tables rather than combining results?
o: Matches values in specific fields to link related data from tables storing different kinds of data
Stacks rows of results storing the same kind of data
mc.e: Joining links related tables side by side; combining stacks similar results.
mc.ez: 连接按字段值配对不同种类的相关表。

mc.q: Which best describes a view?
o: A sorted index of a field
A copy of a table stored separately
A virtual table defined by a SQL statement that does not store its own data
mc.e: A view works as a virtual table referring to data from other tables.
mc.ez: 虚拟表，不储存数据。

mc.q: After UPDATE STUDENT SET SCORE2 = SCORE2 + 10 WHERE SID = '03369', what should be done to the view SCORESHEET built on STUDENT?
o: Nothing; the view shows the new data automatically
mc.e: A view refers to data from other tables; it needs (and should get) no manual update.
mc.ez: 不用做任何事。

mc.q: Why must calculated fields like SCORE1*0.4+SCORE2*0.6 be given an alias in a view?
o: To make it a primary key
So that the field can be selected easily later
Otherwise the view cannot be created in any DBMS
mc.e: Without an alias, selecting the calculated column from the view is hard.
mc.ez: 方便之后选取。

mc.q: COUNTCLUB is created by SELECT SID, COUNT(*) AS CLUBNUM FROM SC GROUP BY SID. A student who joins no club:
o: does not appear in the view
mc.e: The student has no row in SC, so the view (built only from SC) does not contain them.

The base table SC is deleted

mc.ez: 引用它的 view 失效。

mc.q: Which is NOT a property of views?
o: It speeds up searching by binary search
mc.e: Binary search on a sorted field is the property of an index, not a view.
mc.ez: 二分搜寻是 index 的特性。

mc.q: Why does MAX(COUNT(*)) fail in most DBMS, and what is a fix?
o: MAX only works on text; use TOP
COUNT cannot be used with GROUP BY; use SUM
An aggregate cannot directly summarise another aggregate; treat the grouped result as a table with an alias, or use ORDER BY … LIMIT 1
mc.e: Use SELECT MAX(TOTAL) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS TOTAL … GROUP BY SID) t, or ORDER BY TOTAL DESC LIMIT 1.

mc.q: An index table for NAME contains:

A copy of all records sorted by every field
All fields of the table, unsorted

mc.ez: 被索引栏位改变或新增记录时。

mc.q: Why should only frequently searched fields be indexed?
o: Indices take time to update and storage space to store
Only one index is allowed per database
mc.e: The cost (update time and storage) is only worth it for fields searched often.

pr.task: Tables ROOM(ID, RNAME, CAPACITY) and PATIENT(ID, PNAME, SEX, WEIGHT, HEIGHT, RID). First create view RPNUM showing each room's ID, RNAME, CAPACITY and number of patients PNUM (rooms with no patients show 0). Then, in the same answer, query the view to list the RNAME of each room with a free bed (PNUM < CAPACITY). Your last statement must be the SELECT.
pr.taskz: 先建立 view RPNUM（每间房的 ID、RNAME、CAPACITY 和病人数 PNUM，空房为 0），再查询该 view 列出有空床的房间名称。最后一句必须是 SELECT。

check.expected_sql: SELECT RNAME FROM ROOM r WHERE CAPACITY > (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM PATIENT WHERE RID = r.ID)

pr.solution:
CREATE VIEW RPNUM AS SELECT r.ID, RNAME, CAPACITY, COUNT(p.ID) AS PNUM FROM ROOM r LEFT JOIN PATIENT p ON r.ID = p.RID GROUP BY r.ID;
SELECT RNAME FROM RPNUM WHERE PNUM < CAPACITY

pr.tz: 按性别的最低 BMI（视图）
pr.task: Using PATIENT and ROOM, create view PBMI with each patient's ID, PNAME, SEX, BMI (WEIGHT/HEIGHT/HEIGHT) and RNAME, keeping patients without a room. Then query the view for each SEX with the lowest BMI. Your last statement must be the SELECT.
pr.taskz: 建立 view PBMI（ID、PNAME、SEX、BMI、RNAME，保留没有房间的病人），再查询每个性别的最低 BMI。最后一句必须是 SELECT。

check.expected_sql: SELECT SEX, MIN(WEIGHT/HEIGHT/HEIGHT) FROM PATIENT GROUP BY SEX

pr.solution:
CREATE VIEW PBMI AS SELECT p.ID, PNAME, SEX, WEIGHT/HEIGHT/HEIGHT AS BMI, RNAME FROM PATIENT p LEFT JOIN ROOM r ON RID = r.ID;
SELECT SEX, MIN(BMI) FROM PBMI GROUP BY SEX

pr.tz: 选择要建立索引的栏位
pr.task: An online shop table ORDERS(OID, CUSTID, ODATE, NOTE) receives thousands of orders per hour. Staff search orders by CUSTID many times a day; NOTE is never searched. Write a statement to index the suitable field and explain why NOTE should not be indexed.
pr.taskz: 网店 ORDERS 表每小时有数千张新订单，职员每天多次按 CUSTID 搜寻，NOTE 从不搜寻。写出为合适栏位建立索引的语句，并解释为何不应为 NOTE 建立索引。

check.model:
CREATE INDEX CIDX ON ORDERS (CUSTID)
CUSTID is searched frequently, so binary search on the sorted index speeds up retrieval. NOTE is never searched; an index on it would take storage space and time to update on every new order without any benefit.
